answers.notes: I sing and play guitar, and want both to move on together.

note: A demo week for an intermediate player who sings: four practice days of about 30 minutes, the library's intermediate guitar and voice blocks side by side. Each day opens with a breath warm-up, mixes a guitar technique or chord block with a leap or run, and ends with a tune, a harmony line or a solo.

plan.title: Week 1: sus chords, bends and the leaps of a 4th and 5th
plan.summary: Four practice days of about 30 minutes, guitar and voice in turn. Day 1 is hammer-ons and pull-offs, sus chords on D, and the 4th and the 5th. Day 2 is bends that reach the note and five-note runs. Day 3 joins the first two positions of the scale and sings the octave. Day 4 sings a harmony line, plays chord tones over Am F C G and ends with a solo.
plan.progress:
Techniques: hammer-ons and pull-offs in stages. Next: fingers 2 and 4.
Extended chords: D, Dsus2 and Dsus4; Cadd9, G, Dsus4 and Em. Next: the sus groove in D.
Scales: bends in tune, positions 1 and 2 of the minor pentatonic joined, chord tones over Am F C G, a solo across the join. Next: position 3.
Intervals: the 4th, the 5th and the octave, sung and named. Next: leaps falling.
Runs: five notes up and back, Do Mi Sol Do then a run home. Next: nine notes.
Harmony: two notes at once, a harmony line over three chords. Next: the harmony line, then your own.
Breath: in, hold, out, filled to 80. Next: a long breath out.
